The efficacy of KOSELUGO was evaluated in SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1, an open-label, multicenter, single arm trial (NCT01362803).

phase.text: Phase I/II (Phase II Stratum 1 was the basis for approval)

citations.quote: “A Phase I/II Study of the Mitogen Activated Protein Kinase (MEK) 1 Inhibitor Selumetinib (AZD6244; HYD Sulfate) in Children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) and Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibromas (PN)” (SPRINT), specifically from Phase II, Stratum 1 of the trial.

design.text: Open-label, single-arm, multicenter trial conducted by the NCI Pediatric Oncology Branch

citations.quote: SPRINT was an open-label, single arm, multi-center trial conducted by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Pediatric Oncology Branch (POB).

population.text: Pediatric patients 2-18 years of age with NF1 and inoperable PN causing significant morbidity

citations.quote: Eligible patients were 2-18 years of age with NF1 and inoperable PN that was causing significant morbidity.

endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) — percentage of patients with complete response or confirmed partial response (≥ 20% reduction in PN volume)

citations.quote: The major efficacy outcome measure for the trial was overall response rate (ORR), or the percentage of patients with complete response (defined as disappearance of the target PN) or confirmed partial response (defined as \ge 20\% reduction in PN volume confirmed at a subsequent tumor assessment within 3-6 months).
Fifty pediatric patients with NF1 and PN-related morbidity were enrolled in Stratum 1 of SPRINT.

result.text: ORR per REiNS criteria was 66% (95% CI: 51, 79) by NCI central review; median DOR not reached, with 82% of responders having a DOR of at least 12 months

citations.quote: The results from SPRINT Phase II Stratum 1 demonstrated an overall response rate (ORR) per REiNS criteria of 66% (95% CI: 51, 79) based upon NCI central review.
Among the 33 responding patients included in the NCI assessment, the median duration of response (DOR) was not reached while 82% of patients had a DOR of at least 12 months.

indication.text: For the treatment of pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas (PN)

citations.quote: KOSELUGO is indicated for the treatment of pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas (PN).

target_moa.text: Selumetinib is an orally bioavailable, non-ATP competitive kinase inhibitor of MEK1/2, upstream regulators of the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK pathway; in NF1 mouse models it inhibited ERK phosphorylation and reduced neurofibroma number, volume, and proliferation

citations.quote: Selumetinib is an inhibitor of mitogen-activated protein kinase kinases 1 and 2 (MEK1/2). MEK1/2 proteins are upstream regulators of the extracellular signal-related kinase (ERK) pathway.
oral dosing of selumetinib inhibited ERK phosphorylation, and reduced neurofibroma numbers, volume, and proliferation.

Selumetinib (AZD6244) is an orally bioavailable, non-ATP competitive kinase inhibitor that targets mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)/extracellular signal regulated kinases 1 and 2 (MEK1/2); the established pharmacological class is kinase inhibitor.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 40%): vomiting, rash, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, dry skin, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, pyrexia, acneiform rash, stomatitis, headache, paronychia, pruritus. Serious adverse events occurred in 24% of patients; permanent discontinuation for AEs in 12%. Key warnings include cardiomyopathy (decreased LVEF in 23% of 74 patients) and ocular toxicity (15%)

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (\ge 40%) are: vomiting, rash (all), abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, dry skin, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, pyrexia, acneiform rash, stomatitis, headache, paronychia, and pruritus. (6.1)

Serious adverse events occurred in 24% of patients; those occurring in two or more patients were anemia, hypoxia and diarrhea. Permanent discontinuation resulting from adverse events occurred in 12% of patients
Cardiomyopathy, defined as a decrease in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \ge 10\% below baseline, occurred in 23% of 74 pediatric patients who received KOSELUGO in SPRINT
Blurred vision, photophobia, cataracts, and ocular hypertension occurred in 15% of 74 pediatric patients receiving KOSELUGO in SPRINT.

detail.text: A REMS is not recommended for selumetinib given the current safety profile and the experience of the medical community in managing expected MEK inhibitor toxicities

citations.quote: A risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) is not recommended for selumetinib given the current safety profile and the experience of the medical community in managing expected MEK inhibitor toxicities.
